title: Physical and Cyber Access Convergence
summary: Correlate synthetic badge, zone, login, MFA, and system events without treating correlation as proof of wrongdoing.
objectives: Use synthetic, defensive, authorized evidence to reason about data-center security.
Document uncertainty, safe escalation, and evidence without claiming professional authority.

vocab.def: Give an identity only the access needed for an authorized task.
The decision about what an authenticated identity may access.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: This is a defensive classroom simulation using mock identities, synthetic logs, and offline tables. Do not use production systems, real passwords, secrets, exploit procedures, scanning, bypasses, malware, or packet interception.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Interpret the scenario records, compare identity, role, permission, physical-access, and service evidence, and distinguish observed facts from inference and uncertainty.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Record the evidence source and chronology, identify a safe authorized next step, preserve original records, and escalate to the appropriate qualified role.

practice.answer: It establishes a signal that requires scenario-defined review; it does not by itself establish a confirmed incident.

quiz.question: What is the allowed scope?
options: Defensive synthetic analysis and authorized escalation
quiz.answer: Defensive synthetic analysis and authorized escalation

reflectionPrompt: What was observed, what remained uncertain, and what required authorized escalation?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational security practice, not a cybersecurity, physical-security, or professional qualification.
